extracted.intended_audience: OCS renewable energy developers, lessees/grant holders, auction participants, industry stakeholders, and regulatory/compliance counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluative standards and procedural requirements from BOEM's proposed rule for offshore (OCS) renewable energy leasing, auctions, financial assurance, safety management, and inspections. Useful for parties preparing compliance materials, bids, or comments to the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement and fabrication prior to FDR/FIR
rubrics_metrics.description: The lessee or grant holder assumes any business risk associated with the procurement or fabrication of facility components prior to plan approval or the Department non-objection to the FDR and FIR or the end of the 60-day review period without objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although procurement and fabrication activities prior to FDR/FIR submittal are not prohibited, BOEM reserves the right during FDR and FIR reviews to object to installation of previously procured or fabricated components if inconsistent with accepted industry or engineering standards, the approved SAP, COP, or GAP, or the FDR or FIR, or BOEM's regulations. Developers may opt to delay fabrication until their FDR and FIR have gone through the 60-day review period without objections or received a non-objection to avoid business risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule (publication & content)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes to publish a proposed five-year leasing schedule for the OCS renewable energy program and to update the schedule at least once every two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule would include a list of locations under consideration for leasing, a general description of each area, the calendar year when each lease sale is projected to occur, and reasons for changes made to the previous schedule. As a proposed schedule it would not obligate BOEM to offer all sales listed; BOEM may adjust the schedule through updates. BOEM seeks comment on the content and timing of schedule updates and how best to provide transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Inflation Reduction Act constraint for wind leases
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will comply with the IRA requirement that, during the 10-year period beginning August 16, 2022, an OCS wind lease may not be issued unless an OCS oil and gas lease sale has been held during the 1-year period ending on the issuance date and the sum total of acres offered in those oil and gas sales is at least 60 million acres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed leasing schedule will be developed in recognition of this statutory restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of the Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule (non-binding; procedural differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule would differ from the Five Year Oil and Gas Leasing Program by being less complicated and not constituting a final action enforceable or challengeable administratively or in courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulations for the schedule would not have requirements for public meetings, comment periods, or iterative proposals and would not include a list of factors beyond those already enumerated in §585.102. Any lease sale covered by the schedule remains subject to applicable regulations including area identification, coordination, and environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-auction reorganization and 'provisional winner' concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce the term 'provisional winner' to describe the bidder BOEM determines submitted the winning bid at auction close, pending post-auction reviews and the lease award reconsideration process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisional winner becomes the winning bidder only upon favorable completion of reviews and appeals. The proposed rule consolidates reconsideration and appeal provisions into a single section while retaining separate review processes for selection of a provisional winner and for appealing other final decisions. The rule would outline obligations between auction and lease execution and change the due date for payment of the first 12 months' rent to 45-calendar days after receiving a copy of the executed lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction processes and flexibility in formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace enumerated auction formats, bid systems, and bid variables with a flexible process allowing BOEM to tailor each auction to circumstances while meeting policy objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PSN would propose the specific format and procedures for an upcoming auction; the public may comment on the proposed format and BOEM would publish final auction format and procedures in the FSN. The process must remain objective, fair, reasonable, competitive, award leases to the highest bidder, and provide a fair return to taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple factor auctions and bidding credits (use and mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may implement multiple factor auctions using bidding credits that assign monetary value to factors or actions demonstrated or committed to by a bidder; bids have a monetary (cash) and possible non-monetary (credit) component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors may include PPAs, eligibility for renewable energy credits or subsidies, development agreements facilitating shared transmission, technical merit, timeliness, financing, environmental considerations, public benefits, compatibility with State/local needs, workforce or supply chain commitments, or other factors identified in PSN/FSN. Eligibility for credits may be based on past actions or commitments to future actions (if BOEM has agreed to terms). If a lessee does not meet commitments underlying bidding credits, the lessee would be required to repay the value of bidding credits received adjusted for inflation; BOEM may also impose civil penalties under subpart N of 30 CFR 550. The FSN would specify eligibility, application process, use, and value of bidding credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example mechanics of multiple factor auction (illustrative bidding-clock example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example provided demonstrates how bidding credits combine with cash bids across rounds so that a bidder with credits can win with a lower cash component when combined credit reaches the asking price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the auction BOEM determines bidder eligibility and credit values per FSN; credits can be awarded for prior actions or future commitments per agreed terms. The example shows calculation of combined bid (cash + credit) and exit/winner behavior across rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of comments on bidding credits and mitigation of impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM seeks comment on the use of bidding credits and multiple factor auctions to advance priorities such as workforce development or supply chain enhancement and on tailoring credits to mitigate adverse project impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM is particularly interested in comments on potential impacts to underserved communities and how bidding credits might promote community benefit agreements or alternative means like lease stipulations to achieve policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on improper or inappropriate bidder communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would explicitly prohibit bidders from disclosing auction strategies and economic valuations of a lease area to other bidders in ways that might prevent the U.S. from obtaining a fair return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal outlines rules BOEM would use to disqualify bidders who no longer meet qualification requirements or who engage in specified improper conduct, and specifies how a disqualified bidder might seek re-qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional winner obligations and remedies for failure
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM would define 'provisional winner' obligations and outline consequences if a provisional winner fails to sign the lease, provide required financial assurance, or tender outstanding bid balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM is authorized to take a listed set of actions if obligations are not met (including offering lease to next highest bidder). Lessees who obtained bidding credits for prospective obligations not ultimately met before a specified deadline would be subject to repayment of credits; BOEM may impose civil penalties under subpart N of 30 CFR 550 for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to re-offer leases when provisional winner fails or lease relinquished/cancelled
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may offer a lease to the next highest bidder if the provisional winner fails to fulfill obligations pre-execution or is unable to execute, and may re-offer areas if a lessee relinquishes or BOEM contracts/cancels a lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule provides clear authority for re-offering leases by auction in such circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of COP-approval supplemental financial assurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose elimination of the supplemental financial assurance currently required before COP approval on the basis that decommissioning liabilities accrue only with commencement of approved activities on the OCS, not at COP approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM would continue to require supplemental financial assurance before OCS installation starts to cover anticipated decommissioning costs. BOEM retains authority to assess supplemental financial assurance on a case-by-case basis under §585.517 if COP approval does, in an unforeseen event, cause accrual of new obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace $100,000 lease-specific financial assurance with 12 months' rent
rubrics_metrics.description: Before lease execution, replace the $100,000 lease-specific financial assurance requirement with financial assurance equal to 12 months' rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures BOEM is adequately bonded during early lease stages since annual rental payment is generally the only financial obligation accrued at lease execution. The rule would eliminate CPI-based adjustment provisions tied to the $100,000 figure and would change limited lease/grant financial assurance from $300,000 to an amount equal to 12 months' rent. BOEM seeks comment on further modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional authorized financial assurance instruments (letters of credit, third-party guaranty caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule would explicitly allow letters of credit and other instruments meeting general requirements in 30 CFR 585.525, allow combinations of instruments, and set evaluation criteria for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may accept instruments not explicitly listed if they meet general requirements. The rule would allow guarantors to cap liability subject to BOEM discretion to approve a third-party guaranty for a specific amount, preserving BOEM's ability to approve instruments and criteria to protect taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged funding of decommissioning accounts during operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow staged funding of decommissioning accounts during a lease's or grant's operations period as a method to satisfy decommissioning financial assurance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decommissioning accounts must be fully funded by the time a lessee or grant holder is obligated to decommission the facility. BOEM may require full funding before installation for high-risk projects; BOEM would approve funding schedules case-by-case. This aligns with common European practice and is justified by different risk characteristics of renewable projects (consistent production, PPAs). BOEM believes taxpayer risk is negligible but retains discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of credit ratings to assess financial strength
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM seeks comment on replacing some current backward-looking factors with credit ratings from an NRSRO or a BOEM-determined proxy credit rating derived from audited financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM believes NRSRO credit ratings (investment grade from S&P or Moody's) would be sufficient indicators to allow a lessee or grant holder to use financial strength to meet assurances. If no NRSRO rating exists, audited financial statements may be submitted and BOEM could determine a proxy rating using models like S&P Credit Analytics. BOEM is not proposing regulatory text implementing a rating threshold in this rulemaking but seeks comment on the concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint and several liability and assignment liability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-lessees and co-grant holders are jointly and severally liable for lease/grant obligations accruing during tenancy, including decommissioning. When a lease/grant is assigned, the assignor remains liable for obligations accrued before BOEM's approval; the assignee is liable for obligations before and after approval and must provide financial assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This joint and several liability reduces non-performance risk if any liable party has adequate strength. BOEM seeks comment on whether to explicitly rely on the financial strength of other liable parties, including current or predecessor lessees/grant holders, when determining the need/amount of financial assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Management System (SMS) requirement and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessee or grant holder must develop an SMS for COP-approved facilities and for SAP- and GAP-approved facilities BOEM deems complex and significant; the SMS must be functional at the start of approved activities and throughout the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMS is defined as a combination of policies, procedures, and control mechanisms to meet safety objectives in a disciplined and continually improving manner. Proposed approach is performance-based, allowing adoption of U.S. and international workplace health and safety standards as the SMS framework. Upon SMS receipt, Department will engage to understand risks mitigated and system function, and will provide transparency regarding necessary information for a satisfactory SMS. The rule incentivizes certification from a recognized CAB (not required) which could make a lessee eligible for streamlined oversight (but not guaranteed).

rubrics_metrics.name: SMS reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two reporting requirements proposed: an annual summary of SMS performance and a triannual report on SMS audit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual report should summarize how the SMS performed normalized to work hours and energy generation to verify functionality and track improvements. The triannual report should summarize the results of the most recent SMS audit, corrective actions implemented, and any changes made to the SMS since the prior report. Data could generate industry-wide safety performance comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SMS for all OCS activities and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee must have a functional SMS before beginning any activity on the OCS pursuant to a lease and must use its SMS for all such activities, including site assessment work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies when an SMS must be functional and used (including prior to SAP, COP, or GAP). It aligns BOEM SMS expectations with industry best practices and coordination with OSHA, USCG, and BSEE to avoid duplicative enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspections to verify compliance and safety equipment installation/operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing regulations state BOEM will inspect facilities and vessels engaged in renewable energy activities to verify compliance with applicable terms, conditions, laws and regulations and to determine whether safety equipment has been properly installed and operated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections are a tool to verify compliance; proposed rule continues this oversight role (further specifics likely follow in text beyond this chunk).
